//: The `ccbridge` agent is intentionally NOT defined here.
It used to carry `permissions: [{action:*, resource:*, effect:deny}]` for
twenty-two tools. Measured against the running server, four sessions, about
one token each:
session with agent:"build"            -> 200, free tier serves it
session with no agent                  -> 200, free tier serves it
session with ANY deny rule, inline     -> 503, free tier refuses it
session with agent:"ccbridge"          -> 503, free tier refuses it
So permission deny and the free tier cannot coexist. Enabling the rules does
not harden the bridge; it disables the model, which is the one thing this
project is for.
The original canary test - which wrote CANARY.txt through the shell tool -
measured the correct symptom for the wrong reason: the key was `agent`
instead of `agents`, so no rule was ever loaded and the default
`*/* allow` ruleset was in force. Loading the rules properly was what broke
it.
The real boundary is structural: the bridge calls POST /api/session/{id}
/generate, a bare completion route with no agent loop and no tool catalog,
so there is no channel through which the model could execute anything.
Verify with POST /api/session/{id}/permission if you want the rules
evaluated - that endpoint costs no tokens.
